answer: Work-trace spiral registration: each new agent identity must publish a verifiable record of prior task outputs, and validators require that record to cite and extend a distinct earlier trace, forming an append-only spiral no clone can fork without replaying real labor. A duplicate identity therefore pays the full compute and time cost of every predecessor task it cites, since copied traces fail signature-linked spot checks against execution logs. This leaves no cheap haven for mass registration and forces sybil farms to regenerate genuine work across a costly tundra of unrelated domains.
